name: 1709 Prairie Avenue: the storey-and-a-half brick stable by the tracks, K12
aka: 1709 S. Prairie Avenue, rear building by the Illinois Central tracks

function.note: Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws a brick building crossed by one X, its sign for a stable, at the back of this lot on its north line where it meets the Illinois Central right-of-way. The 1911 sheet draws a brick building of the same place and size there and letters it GARAGE, a 1911 use that is not read as the 1904 one (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11). So it is built as the house's stable and coach house, the use the 1886 plate gives it: a carriage bay, a loft hatch with its hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. Inferred: neither map is of 1904, and nothing read names a horse or a carriage on this lot.

research_note: T-3308 (a piece of T-1933) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit. The 1911 sheet 20 draws a storey-and-a-half brick building at the back of 1709, on the 1701/1709 lot line, its east wall on the slanting west line of the Illinois Central right-of-way; Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws a crossed brick building in the same place, its west wall on the same line within one of the plate's pixels (0.35 m) and about 9.2 m along the lot line against the sheet's 9.54 m. So it stood by 1886 and in 1911, and is carried to 1904 as standing. There is no alley on this side of the block: the lots run back to the tracks. The building's carriage front is therefore built facing WEST, into the house's own yard, and its back wall faces the tracks. Neither map draws a drive to it and none is built; how a carriage reached it is not recorded. The sheet's east wall slants with the right-of-way, so the building is 15.57 m deep on its north side and 18.41 m on its south; the kit builds a rectangle, and the rectangle built is the largest inside the sheet's outline, 15.57 m deep, so nothing stands on railway ground. The wedge it leaves out, up to 2.84 m at the south-east corner, is recorded in liberty L-k12-1709-stable-3308. No picture of it is known. The draft rules now skip census row s20-1709-r1.

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 rests on two maps either side of it: Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws a crossed brick building at the back of this lot on its north line, at the right-of-way, and the 1911 sheet draws a brick building of the same place and size (the T-1840 census rules it present, census row s20-1709-r1, as the district draft did). Nothing read dates it more closely or says it was rebuilt between them. FROM: the record claims the 1904 target and no earlier day. TO: the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

position.symbolic_location: 1709 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: by the Illinois Central tracks, its north wall on the 1701/1709 lot line, parcel prairie_1709 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The middle of the building's west wall (its carriage front, facing the house's yard) at grade, read off the committed sheet 20 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_20.jpg) at pixel (4718.65, 4279.08): the west wall's line by a median darkness profile over rows 4220-4340 (peak at column 4718.65), halfway between its north wall line (row 4185.18, a profile over columns 4760-4900; the 1701/1709 lot line west of the building reads row 4183.93 on the same rule, so the wall is on the lot line) and its south wall line (row 4372.97, columns 4760-4950), each peak refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json): local E 1461.767, N -3104.746. The bearing is the parcel's (prairie_1709, data/street_grid/1904.json, -0.391 degrees, as the draft stood it). The fit's own residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is pixel (4718.65, 4279.08) of the committed sheet 20 raster carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, and the note carries the pixel and the result so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: About the middle of the west wall, u east (toward the tracks) and v north. The sheet draws the building from its west wall line (pixel column 4718.65) and from its north wall line, on the lot line (row 4185.18), to its south wall line (4372.97): 187.8 pixels at the sheet's 0.050779 m a pixel, 9.536 m along the west wall. Its east wall is the right-of-way's slanting line, read at seven rows and fitted on the five clear of the lettering (columns 5041.6 at row 4240 to 5078.9 at row 4365, 0.298 pixels east a pixel south): 15.571 m deep along the north wall and 18.415 m along the south. The rectangle is the largest inside that outline, 15.571 m deep; the wedge east of it, 0 m wide at the north wall and 2.84 m at the south, is not built (liberty L-k12-1709-stable-3308).

stories.note: '1½' lettered on the building: a storey and a half. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a half-storey loft whose walls rise 1.2 m more to the eave (loft_m), so the loft lies mostly in the roof; those heights are RECONSTRUCTED.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with a wall thickness lettered '12' (inches) inside its north wall and again inside its south wall, and the key's fire-wall sign, three ticks, at the east end of its north wall on the lot line. Robinson's 1886 plate also colours it pink, its brick.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storey and a half, the brick and the fire-wall end is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1709-stable-3308. The sheet gives the outline, '1½' storeys, the brick, walls '12', the key's fire-wall sign at the east end of the north wall on the lot line, an open circle printed inside the south-west corner (a key sign this record does not read, and does not build), and no window mark. Turned to the lot: there is no alley here, so the kit's alley wall, with the carriage bay, is the WEST wall, facing the house's yard, and the kit's yard wall is the back wall to the tracks. The party wall stands at the north end on the 1701/1709 lot line, where the sheet puts the fire wall, and the open gable faces south over the rest of the lot. The carriage bay (3.0 m clear), a man door and a stable sash are on the west wall's ground storey, nothing above them: the half-storey's walls (loft_m 1.2 m) leave no room under the eave, so the loft hatch is in the south gable, over a stable door, between two stable sash. Two stable sash light the back wall. A gable roof with its ridge along the west wall at 30 degrees over the 15.57 m span, as the deep stables on the alley across the avenue (1736, 1726) took. No stair, ramp, lean-to, wing, workyard or ventilator: the sheet draws none, and no drive to the building is drawn or built.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and loft are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.
